articleTitle: Dynamic Power Factor Correction in Industrial Systems: An Automated Capacitor Bank Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In industrial contexts, optimizing power factor efficiency is of paramount importance. This work presents a comprehensive study that focuses on the enhancement of power factor efficiency in industrial systems through the implementation of an intelligent capacitor bank control strategy. The methodology employed utilizes real-world data collected from an industrial facility to assess power factor performance before and after the installation of capacitor banks. This approach encompasses motor modeling, algorithm development, and an economic feasibility evaluation. The research findings highlight the significant improvement in power factor, reduction in energy losses, and overall system performance optimization achieved through the proposed strategy, which includes the creation of different capacitor bank stages for achieving the desired KVAR and ensuring the optimal use of capacitor banks.

articleTitle: Formal Modeling and Verification of Validator Voluntarily Exit in Ethereum 2.0 Beacon Chain
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The Ethereum 2.0 Beacon chain is a big step toward improving the security, scalability, and decentralization. It is based on the Proof of Stake (PoS) consensus protocol that maintains the validator status, attestation details, and many more. The term validator is introduced in the PoS consensus protocol and its work is to propose blocks and vote for them by becoming a committee member to add those blocks to the blockchain. We address the problem related to validator’s voluntary exit to vanish its active status and do its formal verification using the SPIN Model checker. There does not exist much research in this area as it was introduced recently in 2020. Further, this is the first work on formal verification of the beacon chain using the SPIN model checker. In this work, we formally specify the validator exit process of the Ethereum 2.0 Beacon Chain using the formal specification language, i.e., Process or Protocol Meta Language (PROMELA). We create a program graph for this process through the SPIN Model checker and describe safety and liveness properties using Linear temporal logic (LTL) in the form of a formula. The formal verification is performed to ensure correctness by giving the program graph and LTL formulas as input to the SPIN model checker whether the properties are satisfied with the program graph

articleTitle: Design and Development of Lab Experimental Model of 3 Degrees of Freedom Moving Tandem Rotors System for Flight Controls
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This research project aims to develop a lab experimental model of 3 degrees of freedom moving tandem helicopter plant as a platform for studying and analyzing flight control systems through wireless communication. The project involves creating a MATLAB GUI application for Bluetooth serial communication, controlling set values and PID gains for system control. The scope includes designing, fabricating, and integrating mechanical and electrical components for the experimental model. Through a Bluetooth interface, the hardware connects to MATLAB software. The experimental model successfully replicates the dynamics of a moving tandem helicopter, with an effective PID controller stabilizing its motion. Results validate the implementation of the flight controller demonstrating the potential of using simple AVR devices for real-time PID operations. This work advances flight control technologies for tandem rotors systems, providing a valuable tool for research and experimentation. Wireless simulation control and remote operation of infield devices using a PID controller for the aviation industry are possible outcomes. Further extensions can be explored, including 6-DOF models and other Bluetooth applications.

articleTitle: Quantum Resistance Group Key Management for IoTs
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Group communication plays a vital role in our interconnected society, facilitating efficient and secure data exchange among multiple endpoints. The issue pertains to the intricate nature that emerges within the limited settings of the Internet of Things and sensor networks. GKM plays a crucial role in maintaining security in group communication schemes. Existing GKM schemes commonly rely on public-key cryptography, which may be susceptible to potential threats posed by quantum computers. This study investigated the usage of post-quantum GKM schemes in the realm of IoTs. To enhance communication security and efficiency in the era of quantum computing, we made significant progress in implementing a post-quantum GKM scheme. Specifically, we have chosen the SABER Key Encapsulation Mechanism, which is one of the four finalists in the National Institute for Standards and Technology (NIST) process. We also present preliminary simulation results for our scheme.

articleTitle: 3D Shape Reconstruction Using Focus Clue From Defocus Blur Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: 3D shape reconstruction has numerous applications in computer vision. Shape from focus (SFF) is one of the 3D shape reconstruction techniques that employs the focus information of the images. Accurate estimation of the focus values of image pixels is a critical step in SFF such that it plays a significant role in determining the overall quality of the reconstructed 3D shape. Traditionally, in SFF, hand-crafted focus measure (FM) operators are used, which do not perform well under diverse and complicated situations. In this work, we propose to exploit the pre-trained deep convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model to estimate the focus values of image pixels. Experimental results showed that the proposed method yields better focus measurements which leads to high-quality shape reconstruction. This opens a window for a vast variety of deep learning-based single image focus/defocus estimation techniques to be employed for the 3D shape reconstruction in SFF.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Six Degree of Freedom Machining Bed
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Machining is the term that refers to the removal of material to obtain the desired shape and size. The current machine removal technologies allow quick material removal but this affects the accuracy and precision of the workpiece. Limiting the tool’s range of motion while allowing the workpiece to move is one way to address this issue. The suggested mechanism is a parallel manipulator that offers the workpiece six degrees of freedom. The mathematical formulation of the dynamics model for the machining bed mechanism and the design of a controller to reduce the error in manipulator leg trajectory are both covered in this study. The outcomes support the use of a six-DOF machining bed for required motions.

articleTitle: Addressing Power Quality Issues through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Power quality (PQ) issues refer to the different types of distortions in the sinusoidal voltage waveforms in electric power systems, also known as “power quality disturbances”. These disturbances can cause many severe problems, including losses in power supply and damage to the electrical equipment; hence, their timely detection and prevention are crucial. The first step in addressing these issues would be to identify the disturbance correctly; a total of 29 types are considered for this task. In this paper, we take some popular pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) based on deep algorithms in MATLAB environment and train them to perform a new task of classifying these disturbances. An integral mathematical model is used to create a synthetic dataset for this purpose, the software version of which is publicly available. Based on the evaluation of the classification performance of these networks, we propose an automated solution to address these quality issues through deep learning.

articleTitle: Optimized Energy Management Considering Renewable Energy and Demand Response in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The escalating demand for electricity, driven by rapid population growth, technological advancements, and economic development, poses significant challenges in balancing energy production and consumption. The arrival of smart grids (SGs) empowers consumers to optimize their energy usage through demand response (DR) programs. This paper presents an optimization energy management framework that utilizes generation from utility and photovoltaic-battery systems to minimize electricity costs, reduce carbon emissions, and mitigate peak to average ratio (PAR). Fur this purpose, the genetic algorithm with crossover variants (GACV) is introduced to solve the complete scheduling problem for scenarios: without photovoltaic-battery systems, with photovoltaic systems, and with photovoltaic-battery systems. To evaluate the performance of the proposed framework based on the GACV algorithm and its different variants, an extensive evaluation is conducted. The objective functions are evaluated and compared for each variant. The highest reduction in cost and carbon emissions are achieved by 48.79 % and 42.7 %, respectively, in scenario II by variant roulette wheel with uniform crossover (RWUC), and PAR is reduced by 41.6 % in scenario III by variant roulette wheel with single-point crossover (RWSC).

articleTitle: Comparison of Bioenergy Production from Different Waste Sources Using Solar-Powered Microbial Electrolysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Hydrogen gas has tremendous potential as environmentally acceptable energy carrier for vehicles. A cutting-edge technology called a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) can achieve sustainable and clean hydrogen production from a wide range of biomass and wastewaters. In this work, the research study has been performed on the “textile industry waste” and “dairy manure waste” to analyze the production of hydrogen gas ($H_{2}$) using solar powered MEC. The experiment is performed by adding different percentages of slurry in the textile and dairy waste (substrates) to analyze the production of hydrogen gas in both substrates. The waste is stored in the containers and an anerobic environment is created by using airtight jars. Then, Nitrogen gas is passed, and the containers are fitted with cathode and bio anode. The test samples have been tested after an interval of 20 days through gas chromatography (GC) for the quantization and comparison of the produced gas for both substrates. The obtained results conclude that textile waste produces more hydrogen gas as compared to the other substrate.

articleTitle: Sliding Tilt Forward Thrust Model and Control Realization for Human Voluntary Motion
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Modelling of Biomechanical systems for human voluntary movements in 3D is an area with very broad range of applications. Human motions like sit to stand is one of the very basic movements that human being need to perform a large number of times in daily activities. In the work presented here, we are escalating our 3D bipedal research to develop 3D Tilt model with forward thrust motion trajectories during sit to stand (STS) of biped. This research enables us to develop reference trajectories for velocities of each joint of Sliding Tilt model. These profiles are the basis for sit to stand (STS) motion profiles for the stroke patients. The developed Sliding Tilt forward thrust model is compared with the zero velocity linear model in order to efficiently model the STS behavior of Stroke patient. The Controllability and Observability investigation of the constructed systems presents that the model, which incorporates sliding tilt with forward thrust is both full rank controllable and observable, hence making it suitable for controller design.

Author Keywords: Human Voluntary Sit to Stand Movement

articleTitle: EMG-based Feature Engineering Approach for Load Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: We demonstrate a machine learning-based Human Activity Recognition (HAR) model in terms of load classification. A self-collected dataset using surface electromyography (sEMG) and BIOPAC MP36 was employed for developing the proposed model. The sEMG signals were obtained while 12 volunteer subjects lifted weights of 1 kg, 3 kg, 5 kg, 7 kg, and 10 kg. In the first step, we utilized an IIR elliptic filter to de-noise the collected sEMG signals. Next, a region of interest extraction technique based on automated relative energy empirical mode decomposition (AREEMD) was used to remove the extraneous data. Then, feature extraction was carried out by employing several pairs of statistical, time domain, frequency domain, and cepstral features. A 10-fold cross-validation technique was used to test the validity of the chosen features on a variety of classifiers, including support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), ensemble, neural network (NN), and K-nearest neighbor (KNN). SVM using a cubic kernel outperformed other classifiers in terms of accuracy, providing the highest classification accuracy of 98.5% for five-class load classification.

articleTitle: Applying Ant Lion Optimization Technique to Enhance Power Converters Performance via Effective Controller Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The electrical power industries are constantly seeking innovative ways to improve the reliability and efficiency of the power network while simultaneously grappling with increasing energy demands and technical challenges. Recent advances in the field of metaheuristic algorithms have given researchers powerful tools to address different power system problems. Among these breakthroughs, the Voltage Source Converter (VSC) stands out, capitalizing on advancements in power electronics and semiconductor technology. VSCs offer enormous potential for ushering in smart grids, integrating renewable energy, and facilitating High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission systems. Conventionally, the manual tuning of Proportional-Integral Derivative (PID) for VSCs has relied on a trial-and-error approach or the expertise of design engineers. This manual approach often fails to achieve optimal performance. The complexity is further amplified when dealing with multiple grids, such as VSC-based Multi-Terminal DC (MTDC) grids. This research article focuses on the application of the Ant Lion Optimization (ALO) technique to fine-tune VSC control parameters. The improved results in dynamic response when these controllers encounter faults and unequal loads. To assess the effectiveness of this novel approach, a four-terminal Multi-Terminal High-Voltage Direct Current (MTDC) system is constructed within the PSCAD/EMTDC software environment. In a direct comparison with the classical tuning method, the proposed technique is subjected to various fault and unequal load scenarios. Through this comprehensive evaluation, the article aims to highlight the superior performance of the ALO-based approach in optimizing VSC controller parameters, resulting in an enhanced system response when faced with challenging operational conditions.

articleTitle: Forward Thrust Modelling and Control Optimization of Biped in 3D for Sit to Stand
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Modelling of Biomechanical systems for human voluntary movements in 3D is an area with very broad range of applications. Human motions like sit to stand is one of the very basic movements that human being need to perform a large number of times in daily activities. In the work presented here, we are escalating our 3D bipedal research to develop forward thrust motion trajectories during sit to stand (STS) movements of biped in 3D. We have developed forward thrust reference trajectories for angular profiles. These profiles are the basis for sit to stand (STS) motion for the stroke patients. The model used in this study is the one in which one foot is fixed (healthy leg) and other is allowed 01 DOF linear movement (neurologically deficient leg). Afterwards the LQR based separate controller is designed for the forward thrust model. Rigid body bipedal model in 3D is designed in CAD software SOLIDWORKS Corp., whereas, model linearization is done in SIMSCAPE / SIMULINK. Afterwards, the optimal control for the system is developed in MATLAB / SIMULINK. The forward thrust model having 22<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order and it is shown in the results that both healthy and paraplegic extremities follows the reference trajectories.

Author Keywords: Human Voluntary Sit to Stand Movement

articleTitle: Generating Sympathetic Nervous System Alerts Using Electrodermal Activity
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The electrodermal activity (EDA) and electrodermal signal is an appearance of the considerate innervations of the perspiration organs. Electrodermal activity has a set of experiences in physiological research, yet it was not until ongoing years that scientists started utilizing EDA for physiological applications like the appraisal in exhaustion, torment, lethargy, practice recuperation, conclusion of epilepsy, neuropathies, sadness, etc. The invention of new gadgets and usage for EDA has expanded the advancement of sign handling strategies, taking measures got numerically in the form of the EDA. A lot later, specialists found that EDA contains data not just in the moderate changes that the mean esteem speaks to, yet additionally in the quick or phase changes of the sign. The methods that have followed have proposed to give a more modern examination of EDA, past the conventional tonic/physic deterioration of the sign. With numerous analysts from the sociologies, designing, medication, and different regions as of late working with EDA, it is opportune to sum up and survey the ongoing advancements and give a refreshed and orchestrated structure for all analysts intrigued by consolidating EDA into their examination.In this research we use BITalino development board to record the values and statistics of a person provide it to Arduino microcontroller to process it and in case of any emergency provide alert to the provided contact information through GSM module.

articleTitle: Analysis of Direct Torque Control of Induction Motor with Regenerative Braking for an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In this paper, a meticulous MATLAB-based modeling of an electric vehicle (EV) has been performed with a suitable selection of its subsystems to achieve a more reliable and robust induction motor-based drive system. Various dynamics of EVs have been analyzed based on practical driving experiences to achieve the desired speed and torque results. A hysteresis band-based Direct Torque Control (DTC) system has been implemented that generates switching pulses for a three-phase inverter powered by the lithium-ion battery pack. DTC is a simple control technique of Induction motors (IM) that allows us to enhance its transient response with greater torque accuracy by directly controlling its torque and flux parameters without complex coordinate transformations. DTC seamlessly integrates with the regenerative braking systems of EVs that enable energy recovery during deceleration, thus extending the vehicle’s range and overall drive efficiency. The regenerative braking system, along with the four-quadrant operation of the IM has been validated by the results of this model by comparing battery state of charge (SOC) with speed, torque, and power requirements.

articleTitle: Modeling and Prototyping of an Active Suspension System for Automobiles Using Hydraulic Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Comfort, safety and stability are some of the most essential and critical features of a modern-day vehicles including cars, bus and other transportation. The purpose of this research is to achieve these features by integrating an active suspension system. Modeling and simulation of the proposed system is developed, followed by a prototype model. Results are then compared in a virtual simulation environment for both passive and active suspension system using hydraulic actuators, along with the fabrication of an actual model. The results showed that an active suspension system brings about much needed stability and comfort as it nullifies the effect of jerks to an extent where a conventional passive system cannot help. Use of this mechanism can also be appreciated in an ambulance, as it will enhance the ride quality and reduce the jerks to injured patients.

articleTitle: Design of Open Loop Control System for Cask Lid Welding Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The control system design of an industrial welding robot is presented. Its purpose is to automate the sealing process of a metallic cask which welds the lid of the cask on to the body. The actuation and control of the welding machine deals with the components, circuitry, and coding behind it. The components are decided based on the functional requirements, also making it safe in case of failure using Limit Switches. Two Arduino MEGA 2560 boards have been used; one to control the motion, and one to measure electrical parameters. Coding is done on Arduino IDE and the program has been tested by simulating it in WOKWI, an online Arduino simulator. A Graphical User Interface (GUI) was made using the Windows Form App (.NET Framework) of Visual Studios using C# language. The algorithm and the program have been validated using a physical mock-up.

articleTitle: Advancements and Performance Assessment in Air Vortex Engine Technology: Modeling, Analysis, and Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Atmospheric Vortex Engine (AVE), A tool for creating an artificial vortex, operates on the idea of thermal energy transfer in the atmosphere. The fact that the environment is heated from the bottom and cooled from the top is the foundation for AVE’s operation. In this instance, the vortex is created by tangential air admission at the base of a circular wall. Convective vortices in the atmosphere, where mechanical energy is created, are used to transmit thermal energy from a high-temperature zone to a lower one. The process might provide cooling and precipitation, among other benefits, and develop into a significant source of renewable energy. By using less fuel or by promoting upward heat convection, vortex engines might reduce the effects of global warming. It would utilize the hurricane and tornado-causing mechanisms. The geometrical parameters considered in the making of the model provide a decent starting point for future designs. This research also serves as a forerunner for future research and aims to change engineers’ mindsets from inefficient conventional energy sources to more efficient non-conventional, cleaner energy sources.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Control Based Higher Order Dual Output Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dual-output buck converter. The baseline converter is a fourth-order buck converter with an input C-L filter. A dual output is generated with an additional inductor and two switching transistors. The converter is operated in continuous conduction mode (CCM) with three switching modes. The two fuzzy voltage-mode control loops are deployed to regulate the dual output voltages. A logic circuit is inserted to map the closed loop duty cycle commands to the three switching transistors of the proposed converter. The operation of the converter is verified through simulations performed in the MATLAB Sim-Power-Systems toolbox, where the converter’s performance is verified using both the load and line regulation tests.

articleTitle: Enhancing Building Envelopes by Looking into the Energy-Saving Methods: A Computational Analysis of Windows’ Phase Change Materials and Translucent Insulation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Energy reduction is a crucial problem in building load management in Pakistan since residential energy use is mostly focused on providing thermal comfort. Under severe weather, windows, which are infamous for having weak thermal barriers, significantly increase energy losses. Phase change materials (PCM) and transparent insulation materials (TIM), which have high thermal inertia, might potentially reduce energy consumption when used in windows. In this work, three different window designs are compared and examined, and their impact on interior temperature is evaluated using ANSYS Fluent numerical simulations. The study’s conclusions highlight the fact that PCM-based windows show very little temperature change during melting, highlighting their significant potential to reduce energy use. Moreover, PCM efficiently absorbs over 90% of incident heat, highlighting its importance in advancing energy efficiency in Pakistan’s building industry.

articleTitle: Design of Programmable Digital Control Attenuator for Microwave Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: High performance wideband attenuators with variable attenuation are considered to be challenging to design. In this paper, we proposed a cost-effective high performance programmable digital attenuator with frequency range from DC - 30 GHz. The programmable attenuator can be set by the least configurable step of 0.5 dB and a maximum step of 31.5 dB using a 6-bit input code. The efficiency of the device is enhanced by the implementation of a metal housing that mitigates electromagnetic interference (EMI) internally and externally. The performance of the proposed design is validated using CST Microwave Studio and AWR Microwave Office. The results show that the proposed attenuator exhibits a minimum insertion loss of 4.3 dB with a return loss greater than 10 dB over a wide range of frequencies. The proposed programmable digital attenuator can be utilized where high performance, wide operating bandwidth, and cost-effective solution is required to integrate in microwave receivers.

articleTitle: Pattern Analysis for Biometric Authentication using Electrocardiogram Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Recently, biometric authentication based on Electrocardiogram (ECG) has been actively studied as a potential alternative to traditional counterparts. Conventional authentication systems require passwords in alphanumeric or graphical format, which involves the risk of loss, theft, or even forgetfulness. ECG-based authentication is currently one of the hot topics of research to address such shortcomings. Here, we demonstrate a Biometric Authentication system based on ECG by using an infinite impulse response (IIR) filter. ECG signals from 36 volunteer subjects were obtained and de-noised using the IIR filtration technique. Then, we extracted 18 time domain, cepstral and morphological features from preprocessed ECG signals. Next, the extracted features were classified by utilizing various classifiers such as Support Vector Machine (SVMs), K-nearest neighbours (KNNs), and Kernel Naïve Bayes (KNBs). SVM-quadratic demonstrated an accuracy of 99.2%, which is the highest among the various classifiers employed in this work. We expect that our proposed method can be utilized for developing an embedded system, which can be employed for the authentication of individuals with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fault Detection Algorithms for Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Solar energy is a well-known renewable energy source, and in recent years, PV systems have played a crucial role in converting solar energy to electricity. Quick action is needed to resolve any operational problems with PV systems if energy conversion efficiency is to be ensured. Therefore, a reliable method for quickly identifying and fixing problems is essential. This study focuses on fault analysis, including shading anomalies and various fault types, in PV arrays. To address this, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) approach is employed, leveraging its capacity to discern complex patterns. The investigation aims to scrutinize non-linear I-V curve patterns in solar panels, using a range of fault scenarios. The research employs diverse machine learning models, including Decision Trees, Naïve Bayes Classifier, MLP Neural Network, Random Forest, and LSTM, to identify and categorize fault types. The study follows a systematic approach, encompassing data collection, preprocessing, simulation, model development, and performance evaluation. Validation against real PV plant data enhances the reliability of the outcomes. Through this investigation, the study seeks to contribute to the field by advancing fault analysis techniques for improved PV system performance and longevity.

articleTitle: Development of PV Inverter Testbed for IEC-61727 and IEEE-1547 Compliance Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Due to escalating energy costs and the transition towards cheaper and sustainable energy sources, there is a growing demand for rooftop grid-tie Photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, the market is saturated with non-compliant off-the-shelf inverters. This abundance tempts users to opt for cheaper, substandard inverters, compromising both reliability and power system integrity. To ensure seamless integration of inverter with the grid, thorough testing to validate its compliance is imperative. This paper presents an indigenous inverter testing facility in accordance with IEC-61727, IEEE-1547-2018, and IEEE 1547-2020. The setup can simulate real-time abnormal grid events to test under and over-voltage and frequency protection, reconnection time, ride-through capability, anti-islanding detection, phase failure protection, and frequency-watt droop feature.This system has the ability to identify missing characteristics in the tested inverters, particularly focusing on essential protection and grid support features. Furthermore, this paper highlights the issues being faced in electrical system due to adoption of substandard commercial inverters.

articleTitle: Realizing Intelligence in 6G Communications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: 6G and beyond wireless communication are considered revolutionary generation of networks, which is able to fulfil the requirements of fully connected world. Structure of 6G communication networks is tended to be densely deployed, dynamic, extremely heterogenous with tight quality of service and because of this architecture untenability of network operation. Due to this reason, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have emerged as a solution to deploy a fully intelligent 6G network. In this paper, key aspects of 6G communication networks and a review about implementation of AI, ML and DL in 6G communications is discussed. Furthermore, some future research directions in this domain are also given that will help researchers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Intrusion Detection Using Effective Stacking of Ensemble Classifiers With Multi-Pronged Feature Selection Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Information security depends on Network Intrusion Detection (NID), which properly identifies network threats. This work explores simulating a NID system by stacking ensemble classifiers with various feature selection methods. We used the NSL-KDD dataset for the investigation. The binary classification performance integrates all assaults into one class and treats another target variable as usual. Random Forest (RF), Bagging Classifier (BC), and Extra Tree Ensemble (ETE) using Logistics Regression (LR) as a meta estimator. Chi2-square (Chi2) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) are also used for feature selection. The experimental findings suggest that the proposed technique is ideal for developing a classification model with high accuracy and outperforms standard machine learning classification methods. The Chi 2 attribute selection strategy with modest characteristics has the greatest accuracy of 99.84 %. A careful comparison with prior research shows that our technique produces state-of-the-art performance with reduced computing costs.

articleTitle: Operational Analysis of a Power Electronic Converter as a Virtual Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This research is based on the design and simulation of power electronic converter as virtual synchronous machine. Synchronverter is a topology for inverters that can impersonate synchronous generators. The proposed inverter provides a highly efficient technique for the power systems where the renewable energy resources are to be in contact with the main grid and offers a smooth operation of smart grid. Conventional inverters have shown suboptimal performance when confronted with faults or abrupt changes in load conditions, particularly when integrated with the grid. This causes the inclusion of a resolute synchronization unit, commonly a phase locked loop (PLL). The primary function of the PLL is to offer the grid parameters as reference values to the synchronverters, enabling them to operate under the prescribed parameters required for synchronization. However, the focus of this project pertains to a system in which the PLL and synchronverter exhibit robust and efficient operation, consistently achieving the specified synchronization requirements. This research endeavors to assess the effectiveness of this self-synchronized synchronverter within both islanded and grid-connected modes. The results of the system simulation underscore the superior efficiency of the self-synchronized Synchronverter in its operational performance.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Wheat Leaf Diseases for Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-based approach for classifying wheat leaf diseases such as stripe rust and septoria for edge devices. The study used a 407 wheat leaf images dataset with three classes: healthy, stripe rust, and septoria. Data augmentation techniques created more training images once the dataset was divided into training, validation, and testing sets. The classification was done using a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a test set accuracy of 98.77%. The outcomes show that deep learning techniques are effective for accurately classifying wheat leaf diseases using cutting-edge devices, with potential for early detection in the field. Future work can include exploring advanced deep-learning techniques and larger datasets to enhance the model’s performance significantly. The proposed method can be used in various applications, such as mobile phone apps, to quickly and accurately detect wheat leaf diseases in the field. The potential impact of the proposed approach is significant, as it can help prevent crop loss and increase crop yield, leading to a more sustainable and food-secure future.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cardiovascular Disease Prediction via Hybrid Deep Learning Architectures: A Step Towards Smart Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease presents a serious and increasing global health challenge, making a substantial contribution to morbidity and mortality rates on a global scale. This research study presents a novel methodology for predicting Cardiovascular Diseases by employing a, recently developed, metaheuristic optimisation algorithm within a neural network framework. The Coati Optimisation Algorithm (COA) is employed in an artificial neural network (ANN) to enhance the predictive accuracy of outcomes related to Cardiovascular Diseases. The enhanced performance of the COA can be ascribed to its adept utilisation of both exploration and exploitation phenomena. This research employs publicly available datasets pertaining to heart and stroke disorders, integrating two datasets focused on heart disease and one dataset focused on stroke disease. A comparison analysis is undertaken between the proposed COA-ANN and existing approaches, namely Particle Swarm Optimizer based ANN (PSO-ANN), Grey Wolf Optimizer based ANN (GWO-ANN), and backpropagation based ANN (BP-ANN). The findings of the study indicate that the COA-ANN model exhibits the highest level of predictive accuracy. The COAANN outperformed the other three networks, namely GWOANN, PSO-ANN, and BP-ANN, with an average accuracy of 98.43%. As a result, the utilisation of the COA-ANN leads to an improvement in predictive accuracy for these datasets, with an increase of up to 2.64%. Additional assessment metrics, such as F1-Score, Precision, and Recall, provide more insight into the balanced performance of the COA-ANN architecture when applied to imbalanced class datasets. These results prove that the integration of nature-inspired algorithms with cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) is a promising direction for future research.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Nonlinear Control in Tuberculosis Transmission Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a pressing global health concern, as it poses a significant threat to societies worldwide. Researchers have developed various mathematical models to better comprehend TB transmission dynamics, with the susceptible, exposed, infected, recovered, and resistant (SEIRs) model being widely employed. This paper proposes various nonlinear controllers, including sliding mode control (SMC), integral sliding mode control (ISMC), and supertwisting sliding mode control (STSMC), to reduce the number of infected individuals through effective treatment strategies while preventing susceptible and exposed individuals from contracting the disease via vaccination. The gains of the proposed controller have been optimized using improved grey wolf optimization with integral time absolute error as an objective function. The Lyapunov stability criteria has been used in mathematical analysis to demonstrate the asymptotic stability of proposed controllers. MATLAB/Simulink is used for all simulations to compare the performance of proposed controllers. For a real-time scenario, hardware validation is performed using a hardware-in-loop experimental setup with the C2000 Delfino and the MCU F28379D Launchpad.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Power Forecasting in Multi-Weather Conditions Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Renewable energy, with its abundant and sustainable potential, has emerged as a critical component of the global energy landscape. The need for accurate power forecasting is evident due to the demands of integrating renewable energy into existing grids, increasing load management, managing resources efficiently, and reducing environmental impact. To address this need and introduce a new era of even more accurate solar power predictions, this research paper presents a comprehensive investigation. In this pursuit, we introduce an innovative Deep Neural Network (DNN) and thoroughly assess its performance against benchmark machine learning models, including Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), Random Forest Regression (RFR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR). To train and test the models real-world solar power generation data from the Quaid e Azam Solar Park is used. To achieve more accurate models the data is divided into diverse weather conditions sunny, cloudy, and rainy days. Each model is trained and tested separately. The results decisively demonstrate that the proposed DNN outperforms all other models, offering a promising avenue to revolutionize solar power forecasting and enhance the harnessing of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology for Land Registry Management in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Blockchain technology provides a secure framework for dealing with digital assets, conducting financial transactions, and managing property information. The traditional process of land registration often suffers from inefficiency and complexity, primarily due to the involvement of multiple intermediaries, which increases the risk of fraudulent land transfers. In developing countries, property records are often not easily accessible, relevant processes are susceptible to corruption, and have a lengthy turn-around time. This not only leads to disputes over land ownership but hinders the economic activity, such as, disused land, legal complications for agricultural loans and mortgages. By leveraging blockchain technologies, land ownerships can be transparent, supporting accessible and trustworthy land transfers with a reduced risk of fraud and corruption. We propose a blockchain based solution to facilitate access to land documents for verifying land ownership prior to transferring funds from a buyer to the seller. The transparent and unalterable public ledger can thus validate and preserve the land transactions.

articleTitle: Advancing Optimized Nonlinear Control Strategies for Cancerous Tumor Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Cancer presents a substantial worldwide health concern, with its uncontrolled cell growth, invasive nature, and intricate diagnostic and treatment requisites. Exploring this complexity, the nonlinear mathematical models of cancerous tumor cells provide deep insights into their actions and feasible intervention approaches. Researchers have carefully constructed these mathematical structures to enhance our understanding of how cancerous tumors develop, focusing particularly on untangling the intricate interactions among tumor cells, hunting predator cells, and resting predator cells. This paper introduces a variety of nonlinear controllers, with a specific emphasis on integral sliding mode control (ISMC) and integral super-twisting sliding mode control (ISTSMC). The main aim of implementing these controllers is to mitigate the expansion of tumor cells to a non-threatening magnitude, optimize the abundance of hunting predator cells, and sustain resting predator cells at a level equivalent to 40% of the count of hunting predator cells. The controller gains have been meticulously refined through the utilization of a genetic algorithm, wherein the optimization objective is anchored on the integral time absolute error. The mathematical analysis incorporates the Lyapunov stability criteria to firmly establish the asymptotic stability of the introduced controllers. Employing MATLAB/Simulink, all simulations are meticulously executed, enabling a comprehensive and insightful performance comparison among the proposed control strategies. Advancing beyond the realm of simulation, real-time validation entails a hardware-in-loop experimental configuration, seamlessly integrating the capabilities of the C2000 Delfino alongside the MCU F28379D Launchpad.

Author Keywords: integral super twisting sliding mode control

articleTitle: Acceleration of Digital Education in Pakistan during pandemic (COVID-19): A case study based on ML
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This research examines the rapid evolution of DE in Pakistan, specifically during the COVID-19 pandemic. Study shows that consistent allocation of resources to enhance digital literacy would significantly enhance the quality of the learning process. The research uses statistical analysis and machine learning algorithms to explore DE’s impact, challenges, and prospects in education. A quantitative approach is a case study methodology involving a questionnaire survey of 300 students across diverse Pakistani educational institutions. Ethical considerations ensure privacy protection by excluding intrusive queries. The data collected includes categorical and ordinal variables, covering aspects like gender, institute type, preferred platforms, satisfaction levels, and difficulty perceptions. The study uncovers insights into the acceleration of DE, revealing student preferences and pandemic-related experiences. Challenges posed by technology and remote learning are highlighted, with poor internet connectivity emerging as a significant hurdle. This research informs policy decisions for crisis-driven education reforms, contributing to improved remote learning quality. Analyzing the accuracy of machine learning algorithms provides predictions of DE trends. The study fosters a comprehensive understanding of Pakistan’s DE landscape, fostering future enhancements and innovations in remote learning strategies.

articleTitle: Feasible Selection of Candidate Wind Farms’ Capacity for Generation Expansion Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The urgency of accelerating progress toward universal energy access can’t be overstated as it influences every social, economic, and environmental goal. After exploring the environmental benefits of wind power, its role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and mitigating climate change, system operators are planning to increase generation by installing new capacities of wind power projects. This study focuses on the comprehensive analysis of a wind farm’s expansion, covering various aspects such as technical considerations, financial analysis, and feasibility assessment. The stochastic wind speed data of 24 hours is modeled by Profiles in Matpower Optimal Scheduling Tool for real-world wind scenarios across a year. The wind speed data used for assessing wind capacity utilization belongs to Jhimpir Sindh Pakistan. This wind speed data is incorporated in the standard IEEE 30 bus network with a 20% increased load demand. The analysis of case studies by considering candidate capacities through multiperiod stochastic Optimal power flow in Matpower Optimal Scheduling Tool reveals the most feasible capacity of wind generation to be installed in the future. The wind farm’s feasibility depends on wind resource availability, resource utilization, grid connections, and load demand. Furthermore, the project’s financial viability is analyzed by assessing the initial investment, the time required to recover the investment, and, the profit. The feasible generation expansion approach offers an alternative planning strategy. As it provides a comprehensive understanding of the technical, financial, and environmental aspects of generation expansion planning, offering valuable insights to support informed decision-making and contribute to a sustainable and clean energy future.

articleTitle: Optimum Load Forecasting Model-Based Intelligent Residential System Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Accurate load forecasting has become a challenge due to the unpredictable behavior of microgrid systems. As researchers and industries implement eco-friendly intelligent residential systems, there is a need to address energy consumption issues brought on by erratic human activity and weather. A self-sufficient and intelligent green residential network has been proposed to tackle this. This system uses machine learning to predict energy load by analyzing real-time data and considering renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic, wind power, and energy storage. The proposed energy management and load forecasting optimization model is based on machine learning algorithms. Specifically, the non-linear auto-regressive exogenous neural network has shown to be the most accurate at predicting future loads with an error rate of only 0.226%. Various machine learning algorithms were analyzed to determine the optimal load forecasting solution.

articleTitle: ANN-based optimized robust nonlinear MPPT algorithm for bidirectional quadratic converter in a PV system
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: As the demand for energy continues to rise, traditional fossil fuel reserves are depleting rapidly. Solar energy has garnered significant attention in sustainable energy systems due to its widespread appeal and potential. The output of photovoltaic systems fluctuates due to changes in factors like load requirements and atmospheric conditions hence the efficiency of photovoltaic energy is often hindered. To address this challenge, the pursuit of achieving optimal electricity production through the technique of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is used. Due to the inherently nonlinear nature of PV systems, non-linear controllers are better suited for MPPT. The effectiveness of a PV system is intricately linked to the efficiency of the DC converters employed. The quadratic buck-boost converter boasts a broader voltage conversion range in contrast to the conventional buck-boost converter. This expanded range enhances its ability to adjust to fluctuating sunlight conditions, resulting in more effective extraction of power from PV panels. Artificial intelligence have emerged more valuable MPPT approaches and have gained widespread prominence. A robust controller is essential to guarantee effective maximum power point tracking, because the system’s nonlinearities are adapted. The aim of this paper is to employ the MPPT method utilizing Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and the non-linear condition-based super twisting sliding mode (CST-SMC) control to supervise the PV voltage reference up to a desired threshold value. A crucial application involves employing a pre-trained artificial neural network offline to establish the reference for peak power voltage. The experimental outcomes conducted through a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) setup authenticate the real-time efficacy of the suggested controller.

articleTitle: Investigating Optimum Impacts of High Concentration of Renewable Energy Sources in Conventional Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Energy needs have climbed drastically over the last two centuries because of the transportation and industry sectors and the massive migration towards urban areas. Green energy solutions are the answer to meeting the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting global warming and reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. This further boosts the public-private participation of renewable energy sources (RES) in national and international markets. With all these benefits, the unplanned and arbitrary placement of these static generation sources into conventional power distribution systems has several critical impacts on the system’s operation, performance, control, reliability, and sustainability. This paper presents a detailed investigation of the effects of high concentrations of RES on the conventional power distribution system. Stochastic iterative techniques are used to analyze the dynamic response of traditional conventional power distribution systems under normal and transient conditions, and harmonic analysis is used to evaluate the impacts of a high concentration of RES.

articleTitle: Thermal and Experimental Investigation of Eruca Sativa as Potential Alternative to Mineral Oil for High Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This research paper presented a comprehensive experimental study aimed at evaluating the dielectric properties of Eruca Sativa (ES) oil. It also explored the impact of temperature on Dielectric Strength with the objective of establishing ES oil as a viable alternative to the conventional use of mineral oil, which has been prevalent for centuries. The properties assessed in this study encompassed viscosity, moisture content, specific gravity, acidity levels, flash point, and pour point, all of which were examined in strict accordance with IEC/ISO standards. The AC breakdown voltage, denoted as the breakdown voltage of ES oil, was measured using Mushroom-Mushroom electrodes, featuring a standardized 2.5 mm spacing between them. Vegetable oils had garnered attention as promising alternatives to mineral oil due to their superior dielectric properties, physical characteristics, biodegradability, and significantly higher flash point. The findings of this investigation indicated that the dielectric properties of ES oil closely aligned with those of mineral oil. Importantly, the study highlighted that temperature fluctuations had a notable effect, leading to a significant decrease in dielectric strength of ES oil. Furthermore, when considering factors such as environmental impact, lifespan, biodegradability, and overall utility, the cost-to-benefit ratio of ES oil emerged as highly favorable compared to that of mineral oil. This research underscored the potential of ES oil as a sustainable and efficient alternative to mineral oil.

articleTitle: The Applications Of Artificial Intelligence In Data Science, Big Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, GIS and Nanotechnology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence made possible novel opportunities used for assessment creation in businesses, industries, communities, as well as society. Researches have shown that technology is essential within several aspect of life. This factor has led to it being primarily incorporated within numerous enterprises as well as sectors. The uses of AI are infinite to list that was done. The applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in data science, big data analytics, cybersecurity, geographic Information System (GIS) & Nanotechnology are discussed.

articleTitle: Least Cost Transmission Expansion Planning considering N-1 Security Criteria using Discrete Water Cycle Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Transmission Expansion Planning (TEP) is a pivotal aspect of power system development, strategically locating, scheduling, and quantifying new transmission lines within the current infrastructure to meet future electricity demands. TEP involves a comprehensive analysis of technical, operational, regulatory, and economic considerations. Its chief aim is to harmonize a reliable power supply with cost-effective strategies for expanding the transmission infrastructure. TEP strives for efficient electricity supply, emphasizing security and reliability despite N-1 contingency criteria. Recent global blackouts have amplified concerns regarding power system security. Traditional TEP uses AC load flow equations, which can be complex for large-scale cases, leading to the adoption of less precise DC load flow models for computational efficiency. Numerous optimization methods, including mathematical and meta-heuristic approaches, have been explored to address TEP challenges, aiming for optimal solutions in line placement, expansion, and cost minimization. This study introduces an innovative approach, utilizing the Discrete Water Cycle Algorithm (DWCA) for TEP optimization, with a strong emphasis on integrating N-1 contingency criteria. The DWCA optimizes line placement and expansion plans while factoring in investment and operational costs. Its performance is enhanced by introducing stochastic selection of crossover and mutation operators. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated on the Garver 6-bus test system. The results unequivocally exhibit the superiority of DWCA over other methods, resulting in cost reductions and the formulation of optimal transmission expansion plans. This study underscores the importance of DWCA in addressing TEP challenges and offering efficient, cost-effective solutions in the face of growing electricity demand and potential security criteria.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Wireless Communication in 6G: A Review of Current Trends and Developments
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The ongoing emergence of AI-enabled wireless communication holds great promise for 6G networks, ushering in a new era of smart intelligent connectivity and communication, but it also raises some challenges that are related to the privacy and security of users. A lot of efforts are being made to develop advanced security mechanisms, algorithms, and techniques that are responsible for the integrity of wireless communication in 6G, but with the advancement of rich data analysis and big data computing power technology, it would be easy to tackle these challenges by leveraging artificial intelligence. In this paper I have discussed a previous related work of 6G and AI with its previous prominent work, also I have suggested an architecture for advanced 6G that enabled AI, its applications, features, techniques, and technology. It also highlights its challenges, research, and development in privacy and security of data with ongoing impact. I also highlight some of the future trends and suggest some important work that needs to be implemented in this field for future developments.

articleTitle: Formal Verification of Blockchain and IoT-based E-Voting System Using SPIN
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: E-voting systems is great step toward maintaining democracy of countries because they are providing security, privacy, accessibility and fast countability. Blockchain and Internet of Things (IoT) increase further reliability because Blockchain makes voting more transparent and immutable. A mistake like alteration of results, miscounting and less privacy in system can cause huge loss of money, time, faith and effort of human beings. To tackle these errors our system must be correct. Therefore, we address problem related to correctness of e-voting system and try to ensure correctness using SPIN model checker by doing its formal verification. E-voting system are proposed with many different approaches in different studies and those system verifications are done using different model checking tools. But no one has used SPIN model checker in the area of e-voting system verification. In this work, we formally specify the e-voting system using the formal specification language, i.e., Process or Protocol Meta Language (PROMELA). We create a program graph for this process through the SPIN Model checker and describe safety properties using Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) in the form of a formula. The formal verification is performed to ensure correctness by giving the program graph and LTL formulas as input to the SPIN model checker to check whether the properties are satisfied with the program graph.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review of Latest Cloud Forensic Frameworks, Tools and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Background: Cloud computing is widely used in this era of IoTs. Cloud users utilize cloud computing to access various cloud services. The defects in cloud services are exploited by suspicious actors. On the other hand, cloud forensics help against such suspicious actors. It has been observed on many occasions that cloud services were not well designed. Objective: Cloud computing with its services exposed to cyber threats, due to the bad implementation of cloud services, helps suspicious actors to exploit vulnerabilities in the cloud environment. The main objective is to identify different cloud forensic frameworks. Method: We have used the method of systematic literature review to find and analyze different research studies, which mainly are published between 2010-2022. Results: In this paper, we have discovered 36 different cloud forensic frameworks, with some forensic tools. In this SLR we also mentioned some challenges of cloud forensics with recommendations. Conclusion: This systematic literature review unveils the latest developments in cloud forensic frameworks, tools, and challenges. The insights provided in this paper will serve as an invaluable resource for future researchers in this domain, facilitating the enhancement of cloud security practices.

articleTitle: A Secure BlockChain Based Application For Health Records
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: In today’s world, blockchain technology has become a cutting-edge solution for safeguarding users’ sensitive and private information. This technology serves a crucial role in various fields, including artificial intelligence, supply chain management, cloud computing, and notably, the healthcare sector. In healthcare, blockchain offers several advantages, such as confidentiality, decentralization, security, and privacy. It has a significant impact on the industry, especially with the increasing use of Internet of Things (IoT) devices that connect with healthcare systems. These devices communicate with healthcare software, bridging the gap between healthcare and information technology. The introduction of blockchain-based IoT systems has notably improved security, privacy, transparency, and overall efficiency in healthcare. This, in turn, has created better business opportunities in the industry. Traditional healthcare systems have long grappled with security and privacy issues, including challenges like phishing, identity theft, and other security breaches. To address these concerns, a secure blockchain-based application has been developed. This application acts as a bridge between the core blockchain network and application entities, including hospitals, patients, doctors, and IoT devices. Its objective is to create and verify medical certificates. In addition to this, this application ensures various security features, including maintaining confidentiality, authenticating users, and implementing access controls. It achieves this through the use of smart contracts, which are self-executing contracts with predefined rules. Through comparative and performance analysis, it becomes evident that this proposed solution offers a more effective approach compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Smart Meters and their Application for Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Due to technological innovation and more digitalization in this modern era, conventional electromechanical energy meters are being replaced with smart energy meters by power utilities all around the globe. A safe and efficient energy system requires permanent communication among consumers and generators. Ministry of Power is also encouraging the DISCOs to install such smart meters to all industrial and commercial consumers by June 2023. A country like Pakistan which is facing power deficit from last 02 decades can forecast its load demand with the help of data collected via smart meters. Bulk amount of data collected needs to be processed with advanced techniques for accurate load forecasting. Smart metering enables the use of data-driven algorithms for various power system operations and planning functions like load forecasting, future network expansion and up gradation plan. A study of short term load forecasting with the help of classical methods and machine learning method for load modeling of domestic consumers of an area has been done in this research work. The performance of methods has been compared using standards; mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), root mean squared error (RMSE) and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> rating. A SWOT analysis of smart metering prospective for Pakistan Power System has also been carried out in this work.

articleTitle: Computational Analysis of a UAV Drone with Varying Angle of Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This study examines the aerodynamic properties of a tandem-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and applies computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis to optimize its design for increased lift, decreased drag, and improved stability, as well as the assessment of the influence of design parameters on lift and drag. At a specified altitude of 300 meters above sea level, the study builds a 3D CFD model in Solidworks and refines it with ANSYS CFX to simulate the behavior of the UAV under various flight scenarios. The model’s performance is maximized by a well-designed mesh that spans various angles of attack to investigate the relationship between aerodynamic characteristics and angle of attack variations. The results lay the groundwork for future UAV aerodynamics research and provide insightful information for enhancing tandem-wing UAV designs and overall flight performance. Notably, the study highlights energy and momentum imbalances and turbulence as angle of attack increases, emphasizing the importance of accurately modeling turbulence and flow separation through advanced numerical methods.In summary, this research employs CFD analysis to optimize a tandem-wing UAV’s design, aiming to enhance its aerodynamic performance. It utilizes a 3D CFD model, simulating various flight conditions and angles of attack, uncovering important insights for improving UAV design and emphasizing the need for accurate modeling of turbulence and flow separation for a comprehensive understanding of energy and momentum transfer within the system.

articleTitle: Discrete Wavelet Transform for Laser Diode Self-Mixing Interferometry Processing for Vibrations Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Optical feedback interferometry, known for its efficient resource usage, contrasts traditional two-beam interferometry. Laser diode self-mixing interferometry (SM) is a prevalent remote sensing approach. Despite providing insights into target and laser diode dynamics, noise compromises SM interferometry’s efficacy. Leveraging time-frequency signal processing reduces noise in self-mixing signals. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the processing of self-mixing laser sensor signals, specifically focusing on leveraging the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) for enhanced analysis. A Wavelet Transform-based Phase Unwrapping Technique is introduced, surpassing traditional methods like the Fast Fourier Transform, especially in handling non-stationary self-mixing (SM) signals. The technique’s key strength lies in its ability to simultaneously retain frequency and temporal information, effectively addressing challenges associated with dynamic signals. The proposed method ensures precise outcomes for stationary and non-stationary signals, marking a significant advancement in laser sensor signal processing. By harnessing DWT’s capabilities, the approach offers heightened accuracy and versatility, shaping the trajectory of SM signal analysis. Incorporating the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for SMI, our study achieved remarkable accuracy improvements. DWT-based processing resulted in an error of 12.77nm as compared to 60.98nm for RPUM, 5.95nm for FFT for stationary signals, and 11.98nm as compared to 64.64nm for RPUM and 1228nm for FFT for non-stationary signals, marking a significant advancement in laser sensor signal processing. Through this work, we provide a transformative avenue for advancing laser sensor research and elevating signal processing methodologies across disciplines.

articleTitle: IoT-based Quality Model in which Blockchain Enabled to Analysis and Provide Medicine to COVID-19 Patients by VDM-SL
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Coronavirus sickness is an infectious disease caused by a recently discovered coronavirus. The epidemic scenario spread quickly over the world as a result of COVID-19. Drones are extremely helpful in combating the COVID-19 outbreak. Drone-based technologies are being studied in COVID-19 pandemic scenarios for managing pandemic crises in various scenarios using real-time and simulation-based scenarios. There is a lot of work out there now, but it’s primarily about analytical techniques and simulation approaches, which don’t guarantee that a system is correct and trustworthy. Many breakthroughs in the implementation of novel technology, on the other hand, are still predicted. As a result, the proposed research will be used the Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain, Unified Modeling Language (UML), and Formal methods to offer a framework for identifying the COVID-19 patient drone-based system. Experts say that the ability of blockchain to validate constantly changing data is one of the main benefits of using blockchain-enabled apps. This capacity could be very helpful in addressing the rapidly evolving COVID-19 issue. VDM-SL has been utilized for formal specification, formal analysis, and formal model verification and validation.

articleTitle: Analyzing EMI-Induced Degradation of HF SDR Receiver Sensitivity and Its Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: This paper examines the vital link between conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) and the degradation of sensitivity in HF SDR receivers. Observing anomalies in sensitivity behavior prompted a thorough examination across five hardware iterations. Focused on the HF frequency range of 1.6 MHz to 30 MHz, encompassing the conducted EMI spectrum (20 kHz to 30 MHz), we unveil how crystal oscillator and power supply harmonics generate unwanted signals within this band. A comprehensive testing regime and strategically planned interventions successfully addressed sensitivity loss. This underscores the significance of precise power supply design in RF electronics, bearing profound implications for enhancing the performance of robust HF SDR receivers in the face of EMI challenges.

articleTitle: A MultiLayer BlockChain Based Framework for Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: With the increasing use of smart devices in IoT networks, ensuring security in communications between these devices has become a major challenge. Blockchain technology, known for its decentralized and secure nature, holds promise in addressing security concerns within 5 G-enabled IoT networks. This research introduces a Multi-layer Blockchain Security model to safeguard IoT networks while simplifying its practical application. They use a technique called clustering to create a multi-layer structure within the IoT network. These clusters are formed using a combination of advanced algorithms, including Evolutionary Computation Algorithm, Simulated Annealing, and Genetic Algorithms. Headers within these clusters handle local authentication and authorization, and they use a private blockchain system to communicate with relevant base stations, adding credibility and security while providing a network authentication mechanism. The widely accepted open-source Hyperledger Fabric Blockchain platform is employed for building this model. In parallel, base stations utilize a global blockchain approach to securely communicate with each other. Simulation results show that this clustering approach outperforms previous methods, and the proposed lightweight blockchain model effectively balances network latency and throughput, offering advantages over traditional global blockchain systems.

articleTitle: Cheetah Optimizer-based Framework for Least Cost Generation Expansion Planning Incorporating Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The long-term Generation Expansion Planning (GEP) includes identification of location, types, and construction period of new power generating facilities which must be included to the existing power system to cater the increasing demand over a planning horizon. GEP is a highly constrained, dynamic, and mixed-integer nonlinear discrete problem in nature. When renewable energy sources are embedded in GEP problem it makes it more complicated and less reliable due to their alternating nature. Many researchers solve this problem with different techniques, but it is observed that metaheuristic techniques can solve this problem in a more efficient way. In this research article a combined technique of Cheetah Optimizer (CO) based Algorithm with Correction Matrix Method with Indicator (CO-CMMI) is utilized to solve the GEP problem along with consideration of Renewable Energy resources. The proposed (CO-CMMI) framework has given favorable results in terms of least cost GEP, generation forecasting, reduced emissions and runtime as compared to results given by recent research.

articleTitle: Impact of COVID-19 on Productivity of Software Engineers: A Comparative Analysis of work from home (WFH) and work from office (WFO) environment using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The abstract of this research study encapsulates an exploration of the transformative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the software and IT industry, specifically concerning the work practices of software engineers. With a significant shift towards remote work arrangements, both partial and full-time, this study examines the resultant changes in productivity. Through a comparative analysis, the research contrasts the preferences and outcomes of Working from Home (WFH) and Working from Office (WFO) modes among software engineers. Data was gathered through a questionnaire distributed to 174 professionals in the Punjab region, and subsequent analysis employed diverse data processing techniques, including machine learning algorithms. The study’s primary goal is to identify the preferred work setup for software engineers, assessing the accuracy of various classifiers in predicting these preferences based on collected data. Notably, the Decision Tree and Random Forest classifiers showcased impressive accuracies of 96.23 %, reinforcing the models’ robustness. The Support Vector Machine achieved an accuracy of 90.56 %, while the Logistic Regression model demonstrated an accuracy of 88.67 %, offering valuable insights. The Multinomial Naive Bayes algorithm yielded an accuracy of 77.36 %, contributing to understanding work preference dynamics. Lastly, the K Neighbors model demonstrated an accuracy of 67.92 %, suggesting potential limitations in capturing nuanced patterns. The abstract briefly overviews the research’s objectives, methodology, and critical findings, including the accuracy rates of various classifiers.

articleTitle: Peer to Peer Energy Trading In Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: The study addresses the current centralized power infrastructure’s shortcomings and focuses on the development of decentralized smart power systems employing microgrid networks. It introduces the notion of peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading, which allows for direct buying and selling of electricity between users without the need for traditional intermediaries such as utilities. This method is especially beneficial in microgrids. The primary purpose of this work is to create a peer-to-peer energy trading mechanism for renewable energy sources, specifically wind turbines and solar panels connected in a microgrid. The model is developed with the IEEE 9 bus bar technology and three prosumers (producerconsumers) from the microgrid network. The trading concept is conceived from the standpoint of the prosumer. Furthermore, the article investigates the integration of blockchain technology into the energy sector and provides a Bluetooth-based wireless communication network for P2P energy trade. A mobile app for Android smartphones facilitates the trading procedure.

articleTitle: Conventional Protection Approach for Microgrids Considering all types of Phase faults for both Grid Connected and Islanded Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Emerging Trends in Electrical, Control, and Telecommunication Engineering (ETECTE)
abstract: Microgrids, now a days are attracting the Power system designer’s interest as they have capability to provide power in island mode by disconnecting from utility grid in case if any major fault occurs to utility. Fossil fuels utilization for power generation is harmful for environment while Microgrids are echo friendly as they encourage the use of Renewable Energy. During the planning of a Microgrids, the Protection design is major concern for their reliable operation. Due to presence of Distributed Energy Resources inside Microgrids the current flow direction doesn’t remain conventional (from utility to load), hence an intelligent protection scheme is required. After the transition from grid connected to island mode the fault currents magnitude drastically changes which affects the protection because the over current relays inside microgrid are set on high pickup current values. In this paper a robust low cost and efficient current controlled undervoltage protection scheme is introduced which use locally measured current and voltage and make tripping decision to ensure the protection under island as well as Grid-connected mode and don’t require any communication channel. This protection scheme is tested on 9-Bus Canadian Urban Benchmark Distribution System developed on ETAP Software.
